title: Synchronizing Cross-Functional Product Discovery
business: A mid-sized product design firm managing complex client discovery sessions across multiple time zones.
problem: Project managers struggle to maintain consistency in product requirements because meeting insights remain siloed in individual note-taking apps, leading to conflicting feature priorities and delayed development cycles.
solution: By integrating the Granola connector with Claude, the team centralizes meeting transcripts into a single AI-accessible repository. This allows Claude to synthesize cross-meeting context, identifying recurring user pain points and conflicting requirements directly from the source transcripts without manual aggregation.
steps: Configure the Granola MCP server using the provided connector URL to establish a secure link between the meeting history and the Claude interface.
Authenticate the connector to grant Claude read-only access to the specific meeting workspaces containing discovery session transcripts.
Utilize the list_meetings tool to identify the relevant session IDs for the current product discovery sprint.
Execute the get_meeting_transcript tool to pull raw dialogue data into the Claude context window for thematic analysis.
Prompt Claude to compare requirements across selected transcripts to generate a unified feature backlog.
outcome: The team achieves a single source of truth for product requirements, significantly reducing the time spent manually reconciling notes and ensuring that design decisions are grounded in actual client feedback.
limitation: The connector relies on the quality and availability of the meeting transcripts; if a meeting is not recorded or the transcript is incomplete, Claude will lack the necessary context, which can be verified by checking the output of the get_meeting_transcript tool for missing segments.
